name: Wavetable warp modes rebuilt as phase-signal transforms (PWM, bend, asym, mirror, sync/window, flip, quantize, remap)
goal: Rebuild wavetable 'warp modes' portably by splitting an oscillator into a 0-to-1 phase ramp that reads the waveform and then transforming that phase signal before lookup: squeeze (PWM), pinch/skew (bend/asym), mirror, overdrive-and-wrap (sync, optionally windowed), comparator-switched 180-degree rotation (flip), staircase quantize, and a drawn transfer curve (remap), so a Web Audio/AudioWorklet or modular oscillator can chain and modulate several warps at once instead of picking one mode.

source.title: A comprehensive guide to phase and warp modes in Serum, Bitwigs Grid and other synths like it

prerequisites: Oscillator whose phase can be driven externally (modular phase input, or a custom AudioWorklet that reads a wavetable at a computed phase)
An oscilloscope/visualiser to view the phase signal and output wave

inputs.name: source_wave
inputs.description: Any original/free single-cycle or wavetable frame (a sine is clearest for learning)

inputs.name: warp_chain
inputs.description: Ordered phase transforms to apply, e.g. [pwm, pinch] or [mirror, skew]

outputs.name: warped_oscillator
outputs.description: Oscillator with one or more modulatable phase-warp stages

steps.action: Model the oscillator as three variables: frequency (set by the played note, how often the cycle repeats), amplitude, and phase (where you are in the cycle and HOW you move from the start position to the end). Warp modes change only the phase motion.
steps.expect: Each warp can be described as a curve of phase vs time within one cycle

steps.action: Separate phase from waveform: generate a linear phase ramp (sawtooth 0->1 once per cycle at the note frequency) and feed it at 100% into the oscillator's phase input/lookup. A straight ramp must reproduce the original wave exactly. (Bitwig Grid: switch off the oscillator's internal phase section and patch a phase module in; Web Audio: AudioWorklet table read at the computed phase.)
steps.expect: Scope shows a saw-shaped phase signal and the unchanged sine at the output

steps.action: PWM: squeeze the phase so it runs through the whole cycle quickly, then holds at the end until the period elapses, then jumps back to 0. Squeezing from one side or from both sides is equivalent once you shift the oscillator start phase. A bipolar version can also stretch/zoom into a small part of the cycle, turning a sine almost into a saw and eventually losing amplitude.
steps.expect: Sine is compressed into part of the cycle; opposite direction zooms toward a near-saw

steps.action: Bend (+ / - / +-): apply a pinch curve to the phase. One direction races to the centre, lingers there, then speeds up toward the end; the other direction lingers at the start and end and runs quickly through the middle. Bend +- has its neutral point in the middle of the knob. Asym = a skew curve that moves the turning point to one side.
steps.expect: Waveform is pinched toward or pulled away from its centre; skew leans it sideways

steps.action: Mirror: run the phase through the whole cycle and then reverse direction back to 0 (a triangle-shaped phase). Raising the amount repeats this faster, almost sync-like. To match a synth whose mirror control moves the two halves closer/further apart, follow the mirror stage with a skew stage.
steps.expect: Wave plays forward then backward each cycle

steps.action: Sync: amplify the phase ramp beyond 1 and wrap anything above 1 back down to 0 so the cycle restarts; more amount = more condensed sub-cycles pushed in from the right. Hard wrapping crackles, especially on a sine; 'window' variants force a zero crossing at the cycle start/end (half window, and full window which extends further toward the ends) to soften it while changing the waveform. A window can only be approximated with envelope-style amplitude shaping if your tool lacks it.
steps.expect: Sync timbre rises with amount; windowed version clicks less on a sine

steps.action: Flip: compare the phase ramp to a threshold value (0-1) with a greater/less-than comparator; use the boolean to switch between the original phase and a 180-degree-rotated copy (split/rotate, then merge/select). The wave inverts exactly where the ramp crosses the threshold, and the knob covers two cycles of this. A plain phase-reverse module is NOT the same result.
steps.expect: At threshold 0.5 the second half of the cycle is flipped

steps.action: Quantize: run the phase through a quantizer so only discrete steps are allowed (a staircase), giving a bit-crusher-like distortion of the wave.
steps.expect: Stepped, crushed tone; fewer steps = harsher

steps.action: Remap: draw an arbitrary transfer curve mapping phase-in to phase-out (e.g. stay at the beginning, then catch up exponentially) with the warp amount as the depth; Remap 2/3/4 apply the shaping repeatedly/repeat the waveform more often. LFO-style shapes can be used as curves.
steps.expect: Drawn curve directly reshapes the waveform; higher remap orders add more change

steps.action: Treat FM as related (it also moves phase, via another oscillator) but separate from warping; keep it in its own stage.
steps.expect: FM stage independent from the warp chain

steps.action: Chain several phase transforms in series (e.g. PWM-style squeeze then pinch, or mirror then skew) and assign each amount to LFOs, envelopes or macros for evolving cinematic motion.
steps.expect: Multiple warps active and modulated at once

verification: With every warp amount at 0 the output equals the clean source wave
Scope of the phase signal shows the expected shape for each stage (squeeze, pinch, triangle/mirror, wrapped ramp, staircase, drawn curve)
Un-windowed sync on a sine produces audible crackle; windowed sync is softer
Flip at threshold 0.5 inverts the second half of the cycle
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth/DAW vendors named in the source video.
Distinct from wavetable-crossfade-morph-modulate-pad (frame crossfading) and spectral-warp-vocode-formant-stretch-smear (spectral modes): this skill is the phase-domain model of classic warp modes.

Web Audio mapping: implement phase ramp -> transform chain -> table read inside an AudioWorkletProcessor; the transcript does not cover anti-aliasing, so treat aliasing control as a separate implementation concern.
